meta_title: Contributing · How to take a piece of OpenDrone
meta_description: How to report a problem, change a board design, work on the firmware, and get credited for it. The practical half of the OpenDrone community project.
title: Designed by ... whoever shows up.
lead: OpenDrone hardware is developed in the open. This page is the practical bits: how to report a problem, change a design and get credited for it.
s1_body: Flew it, bench-tested it, or just read the schematic and found something off: open an issue on the board's repo. A photo, a log file, or a net name is enough.
s2_body: Before you change anything: join the [the Discord](@discord). Every board names its maintainer on GitHub; message them there and talk through what you want to change before you touch a file, because someone may already be working on exactly that. [The roadmap](/roadmap) shows where each product stands.

KiCad files are text, newer KiCad versions ship git integration, but merging two people's edits to one layout is still asking for trouble. Coordination beats merge tools here: one person changes a board at a time, schematics are split across hierarchical sheets so separate sheets can have separate owners.

Everyone else contributes through review, and review is where the real capacity is. A design one person draws can be reviewed by anyone. Small, focused changes land fastest: a connector, a footprint, a silkscreen fix, anything can help.
Merged design changes land your handle in the contributors chapter of the product page. Every product page names who developed the board, maintainer first.
s3_body: The boards run community firmware: Betaflight, AM32 and ExpressLRS. Work there helps every board, not just ours. Start with the [firmware partners](/firmware-partners) page if you want the details.
s4_body: Every product links its source where one is public. The hardware is KiCad, latest stable version, one repo per board, all under [github.com/OpenDrone-hw](https://github.com/OpenDrone-hw). Issues and pull requests are open on all of them.
